rationale.conceptual: The method is DFT-based band structure computation, an established protocol. It demands careful implementation of a missing-row slab model, selection of pseudopotentials, correct k-path choices, and interpretation of orbital character, all needed to reproduce the experimental dispersion trend. It is more than a textbook operation but not a novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline comprises model construction, SCF, non-SCF band calculation, and dispersion tabulation (3–4 stages, with significant process steps). It relies on external DFT software (Quantum ESPRESSO or similar) that must be installed and configured; each step passes data to the next, making orchestration non-trivial.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires setting up a DFT slab calculation of a reconstructed surface with a known structure, running SCF and band structure, then post-processing to identify a specific orbital-derived band and characterise its dispersion. This is a standard computational surface science workflow, non-trivial but not novel; the pipeline has several sequential stages (model setup, SCF, bands, extraction) and needs external DFT software installation, but no heavy data or GPU.

compute_estimate.reasoning: A small slab of ~20 atoms with a modest plane-wave cutoff requires only CPU and a few GB of RAM; the only input data are the structure model coordinates and pseudopotentials, negligible volume.
